text: Eighty banners. Under each one, twelve thousand soldiers. Nearly a million men, marching under one broken promise. It began with a handshake. A truce between the believers and the Romans, exactly as the prophet had foretold. For years, it held. Ports opened. Markets filled. Children grew up without ever hearing a siren. Together, they even marched against a common enemy — and won. But on the day of victory, a quarrel broke out over whose victory it was. Within a week, the treaty was ash. The same ports that had sold them fruit now filled with their warships. The prophet had said there would be a truce with the Romans. They would betray it, and come under eighty banners. Under each banner, twelve thousand. In every city, men answered the call. Farmers. Teachers. Boys too young to shave. Schools emptied. Factories fell silent. On every street, a mother stood at a window. They drove north through the night, toward a valley none of them had ever seen. And at dawn, the two armies faced each other at a place the prophet had named fourteen centuries before.
